comment: Single source of truth for the tabs. App.jsx imports this for routing and
for each page's <h1>; build.sh reads it to emit one real HTML file per
route, each with its own title, description and canonical. Adding a tab is
adding one row here — nothing else needs to know the list.
`path` is what ships in the URL, so treat these as permanent: changing one
orphans every link and every bit of search ranking pointing at it.

faq.q: Is it better to rent or buy?
faq.a: It depends on how long you stay, what the home appreciates at, and what your money would otherwise earn invested. Buying carries large one-time costs — transfer tax, legal fees, and selling costs at the other end — that need years of appreciation to recover. This calculator compares net worth both ways over your own horizon rather than comparing rent against a mortgage payment, which ignores that a renter invests the difference.

faq.q: Does this calculator work for Canada as well as the United States?
faq.a: Yes, and the mortgage mathematics genuinely differs between them rather than only the labels. Canadian fixed mortgages compound semi-annually and renew every few years at a new rate; US mortgages compound monthly and a 30-year fixed never renews. The calculator also handles CMHC premiums and BC property transfer tax on the Canadian side, and PMI, the mortgage-interest deduction and the SALT cap on the US side.

faq.q: Should I pay off my mortgage early or invest the money instead?
faq.a: A mortgage prepayment is a guaranteed, tax-free return equal to your mortgage rate, while investing is a higher expected return that is neither guaranteed nor tax-free. The prepayment calculator solves for the hurdle rate — the annual return your investments would need to clear for investing to win — which is typically a little above your mortgage rate once fees and capital gains tax are counted.

faq.q: Does it account for closing costs and taxes?
faq.a: Yes. Purchase costs include the down payment, land transfer or property transfer tax, and legal fees; ongoing costs include property tax, insurance, maintenance, utilities and strata or HOA dues. At the end, the sale pays selling costs and any capital gains tax, and the renting side pays capital gains tax on its portfolio, so neither side finishes holding an untaxed gain.

No. The calculator runs entirely in your browser, there is no account or sign-up, and nothing you type is sent to a server. Your inputs are stored in the address bar, which is what makes a scenario shareable simply by copying the link.
